$comment: The canonical, machine-readable list of every behaviour deliberately duplicated between scripts/dependency_bundle.py and scripts/erp_lock.py, and its two locations. tests/architecture/test_dependency_bundle.py enforces this file two-directionally: every entry's two symbols must resolve to a real callable in BOTH modules (a stale entry describing something already unified fails), and the set of entry ids here must be a SUBSET of a baseline hardcoded in that test -- this file may only SHRINK. A new duplicated behaviour appearing here without the test's baseline being deliberately widened in the same reviewed change fails the build.
retirement_condition: The consumer-cutover slice adopts scripts/dependency_bundle.py as the sole implementation of every behaviour named below, deletes the corresponding duplicated code from scripts/erp_lock.py, and removes the entry from this file. When 'entries' is empty, the non-growing guard in tests/architecture/test_dependency_bundle.py stands permanently at zero and the private-index-facing security mechanics below have exactly one owner again.

entries.behaviour: Compute the sha256 hex digest of a byte string, used to verify artifact and member content against a published or declared hash.

Resolve an index-supplied href against one approved https origin and path prefix, refusing embedded userinfo, a wrong host, a '..' traversal segment revealed literally or after one or two rounds of percent-decoding, and a literal or decoded backslash.

Scan a set of files for the literal, percent-encoded, and base64 (plain and HTTP basic-auth) encodings of a held credential, refusing outright -- never reporting a vacuous clean scan -- when the credential is empty.

Build the dict of every encoding form (literal, percent-encoded, percent-encoded-with-plus, base64, base64 basic-auth) a held credential could appear in, refusing an empty credential. Found by the unlisted-duplicate detector added in the same change that added it here -- this entry was NOT anticipated when credential-string-scan was first listed.
